items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 multimodal mRoPE positions are passed to a 1D fused QK RMSNorm+RoPE CUDA kernel
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

On NVIDIA CUDA, the Qwen3.5-family full-attention implementation unconditionally selects `fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate` when `attn_output_gate=True`.

The fused kernel accepts only one-dimensional token positions (`positions: [T]`) and loads one scalar with:

```python
pos = tl.load(positions_ptr + token).to(tl.int64)
```

However, Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3.8-27B are multimodal Qwen3.5-family checkpoints. Their image/video prefill path supplies contiguous mRoPE positions with shape `(3, T)`, representing temporal, height, and width positions.

Passing contiguous `(3, T)` positions to the current kernel makes it read only the first (temporal) row. Height and width positions are not applied to their assigned rotary dimensions. This silently changes Q/K for visual tokens and can degrade image understanding and GUI coordinate grounding.

The same defect is present in SGLang v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and current `main`.

## Affected checkpoints

| Checkpoint | Immutable revision | Architecture/config | Affected by this bug |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B` | [`6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B/blob/6a9e13bd6fc8f0983b9b99948120bc37f49c13e9/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` | [`1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B/blob/1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0/config.json) | Multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, interleaved mRoPE | Yes |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` | [`017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json) | Same multimodal architecture and mRoPE config | Yes |
| `Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` | [`207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996`](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B/blob/207bd685a7e3696cfaff12ded7c6a7ea0f88c996/config.json) | Text-only `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, no `mrope_section` | No, not this specific bug |

The affected 27B configs contain:

```json
{
  "architectures": ["Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration"],
  "language_model_only": false,
  "text_config": {
    "attn_output_gate": true,
    "head_dim": 256,
    "partial_rotary_factor": 0.25,
    "rope_parameters": {
      "mrope_interleaved": true,
      "mrope_section": [11, 11, 10],
      "rope_theta": 10000000,
      "rope_type": "default"
    }
  }
}
```

SGLang registers `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` through the same `qwen3_5.py` implementation that contains the fused CUDA dispatch:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L2354-L2366

## SGLang versions reviewed

| Version | Commit |
| --- | --- |
| v0.5.11 reference path | [`612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/612785ffdcaf35552f1ed433a981d596ca9fe900) |
| v0.5.16 | [`fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/fdebc938f7f4d16fe6b9f55dcd9a767cf0899ea1) |
| v0.5.17 | [`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102) |
| latest `main` reviewed on 2026-08-18 | [`63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c) |

The kernel file has the same Git blob ID in v0.5.16, v0.5.17, and the reviewed `main`:

```text
56d442098c02fa289414fecf0958638dd7906d5b
```

## Source-level reproduction

### 1. The multimodal processor constructs three-axis positions

`QwenVLImageProcessor.compute_mrope_positions()` calls `MRotaryEmbedding.get_rope_index()`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/qwen_vl.py#L451-L471

`ForwardBatch` documents the result as `[3, total_seq_len]` and concatenates it along dimension 1 before moving it to the model device:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1128-L1132

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py#L1212-L1253

For image/video tokens, the temporal, height, and width rows are different. For ordinary text prefill/decode they are normally equal, which is why text-only accuracy tests may not expose the bug.

### 2. The VLM passes `(3, T)` positions into the language model

The Qwen3-VL wrapper replaces normal positions with `forward_batch.mrope_positions` and asserts `(3, seq_len)` for multimodal prefill:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py#L1423-L1453

### 3. CUDA dispatch has no shape or mRoPE guard

Current `main` uses the fused path whenever CUDA and the attention output gate are enabled:

```python
if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate:
    q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(
        positions=positions,
        hidden_states=hidden_states,
    )
```

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py#L1147-L1163

There is no check for `positions.ndim`, `MRotaryEmbedding`, `mrope_section`, or `mrope_interleaved`.

### 4. The selected kernel is strictly one-dimensional

The wrapper documents `positions: [T]`, and the Triton kernel loads only `positions_ptr + token`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L107-L114

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/63d783bbe0955237ec41f9ddabf7235ddf04673c/python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate.py#L131-L153

The kernel receives no positions row stride, mRoPE section sizes, or interleaving metadata. For a contiguous `(3, T)` tensor, `positions_ptr + token` addresses only row 0.

## Minimal runtime assertion

On an NVIDIA CUDA machine, add this temporary assertion at the beginning of `forward_prepare_cuda_fused`:

```diff
 def forward_prepare_cuda_fused(self, positions, hidden_states):
+    assert positions.ndim == 1, (
+        f"1D fused RoPE received shape={tuple(positions.shape)}, "
+        f"stride={positions.stride()}, rotary={type(self.rotary_emb).__name__}"
+    )
```

Then launch either multimodal checkpoint and send one image request:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

Expected result with current code: image prefill reaches the assertion with a shape equivalent to `(3, T)`. Removing the assertion silently feeds that tensor to the one-dimensional kernel.

The same assertion can be reproduced with `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`.

## Why existing validation missed it

The fused CUDA path was introduced by PR #28320:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28320

That PR changed two production files and did not add a fused-vs-native tensor correctness test. Its reported accuracy validation used a text Qwen3.5 checkpoint and AIME26. Text positions have equal T/H/W rows, so reading only the first row is accidentally equivalent for that control case.

## Expected behavior

For two-dimensional mRoPE positions, Q/K must use the configured temporal, height, and width positions according to `mrope_section` and `mrope_interleaved`, matching `MRotaryEmbedding`.

The one-dimensional fused kernel must not be called with a two-dimensional tensor unless it is explicitly extended to implement the same mRoPE semantics.

## Actual behavior

On NVIDIA CUDA with `attn_output_gate=True`, `(3, T)` positions are passed to a `[T]` kernel. Only temporal positions are read, so H/W rotary dimensions are incorrect during image/video prefill.

## Suggested minimal correctness fix

Use the fused path only for its documented one-dimensional input contract:

```diff
-if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate:
+if _is_cuda and self.attn_output_gate and positions.ndim == 1:
     q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_cuda_fused(...)
 else:
     q, k, v, gate = self.forward_prepare_native(...)
```

Also fail fast in the fused wrapper:

```python
if positions.ndim != 1:
    raise ValueError(
        f"fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_gate only supports [T] positions, "
        f"got {tuple(positions.shape)}"
    )
```

This is a conservative fix. In the current mRoPE scheduler, Qwen3.6/Qwen3.8 text and decode positions may also be represented as `(3, T)` with equal rows, so this guard can reduce fusion coverage for those models. Correctness should take priority; a follow-up optimization can safely pass `positions[0]` in paths where equal rows are guaranteed without performing a synchronizing GPU comparison.

The complete performance fix is to extend the fused kernel to accept `(3, T)` positions plus the row stride, `mrope_section`, and interleaving mode.

## Tests requested

Please add a CUDA fused-vs-native test using identical Q/K, norm weights, and RoPE cache:

| Case | Positions | Expected result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text control | `[T]` | Fused and native close within dtype tolerance |
| Equal-axis control | `(3, T)`, all rows equal | Either safely reduce to row 0 or use the native path |
| Real mRoPE | `(3, T)`, T/H/W differ | Must bypass the 1D kernel or match `MRotaryEmbedding` numerically |

An end-to-end image grounding regression test would also be useful, but the tensor-level contract test should be sufficient to prevent this silent correctness bug from recurring.

## Scope and current evidence

The source-level shape/semantic mismatch is deterministic and independently reproducible. It confirms a correctness defect in the CUDA path and confirms that Qwen3.8-27B shares the affected configuration and implementation path.

I do not include a controlled end-to-end CUDA grounding A/B in this report yet. Therefore, this issue does not claim that this kernel explains every observed visual benchmark regression; it claims the narrower, directly provable bug that genuine three-axis mRoPE positions are silently processed as one-dimensional positions.


### Reproduction

```
python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \
    --port 8000 \
    --tp-size 8 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

items.title: [Feature] Workload-Signature-Based Parallelism Advisor for Diffusion Serving
items.body:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Extend SGLang Diffusion's current rule-based `auto_tune` and parallelism documentation with an evidence-producing advisor that selects a legal execution topology from a workload signature and a calibrated benchmark record. The current documentation correctly explains that CFG, TP, and SP split different axes and that more parallelism is not always faster. `auto_tune.py` already makes high-confidence memory/residency choices and can enable CFG/FSDP under guarded conditions. The missing layer is a reproducible way to answer: > For this model revision, device topology, latent shape, denoising schedule, CFG mode, and effective candidate batch, which legal plan has the best end-to-end objective without failing quality or memory gates? This matters especially for short-sequence world/action models. A wider TP degree may amortize well for a multi-candidate batch but regress a latency-first single request because fixed collective and host-dispatch costs dominate. #### Goals - Enumerate legal CFG/TP/SP/FSDP/replica plans from model and hardware constraints. - Benchmark plans end to end rather than rank them from FLOPs alone. - Key recommendations by workload signature, not just model name. - Preserve explicit user configuration as highest priority. - Add a true world-size-one serving fast path where distributed work is semantically a no-op. - Produce a machine-readable calibration report and explain every selection/fallback. #### Non-goals - Moving a live request between TP topologies mid-denoising in phase 1. - Automatically renting/allocating GPUs. - Declaring one plan globally optimal for every batch size or objective. - Replacing existing memory-safety checks. #### Data model ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class DiffusionWorkloadSignature: model_revision: str task_type: str latent_tokens: int num_inference_steps: int | tuple[int, ...] logical_batch: int candidate_count: int cfg_branches: int dtype: str cache_mode: str compile_mode: str device_topology: str @dataclass(frozen=True) class ParallelExecutionPlan: num_gpus: int cfg_parallel_size: int tensor_parallel_size: int sequence_parallel_size: int fsdp: bool data_parallel_replicas: int @dataclass(frozen=True) class CalibrationResult: signature: DiffusionWorkloadSignature plan: ParallelExecutionPlan feasible: bool latency_ms: Mapping[str, float] peak_memory_bytes: int quality_gate: str communication_summary: Mapping[str, float] ``` #### Advisor flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Sig["Workload signature
shape, steps, batch, CFG, topology"] Caps["Model + hardware capabilities"] Enumerate["Enumerate legal plans"] Filter["Static feasibility
divisibility, memory, backend support"] Calibrate["Controlled end-to-end calibration"] Gate["Quality + stability gate"] Rank["Rank by selected objective
latency, throughput, or memory"] Record["Versioned calibration record"] Resolve["Startup/request-class resolver"] Run["Selected serving pool"] Sig --> Enumerate Caps --> Enumerate --> Filter --> Calibrate --> Gate --> Rank --> Record --> Resolve --> Run ``` #### Plan enumeration and static filters Reuse existing legality rules: - total devices equal the product/composition required by CFG/TP/SP/FSDP; - attention heads and sequence dimensions satisfy divisibility constraints; - the model/backend explicitly supports each parallel axis; - estimated resident memory and temporary peak fit the least-free selected GPU; - cache/compile combinations are compatible with the plan; and - CFG parallel is proposed only for models with the required branches. Static estimates only eliminate impossible plans. They should not select the winner. #### Calibration protocol For each remaining plan: 1. launch in an isolated calibration mode; 2. run a complete warmup, separating compile/cold-start time; 3. run repeated end-to-end requests at the exact signature; 4. record p50/p95 latency, throughput, peak memory, stage times, and collective counts/bytes; 5. apply the model's accuracy/trajectory gate; and 6. store environment, code revision, model revision, driver/backend versions, and device topology. The advisor ranks only passing plans. A microbenchmark win is supporting evidence, not a substitute for end-to-end measurement. #### Runtime resolution Phase 1 should resolve at server startup or route between separately launched pools. It should not reconfigure process groups for each request. Precedence: 1. explicit user-provided parallel flags; 2. exact validated calibration match; 3. compatible conservative recipe from pipeline config; 4. existing rule-based `auto_tune` behavior; or 5. clear failure if the model cannot fit safely. The log/metrics record which tier selected the plan and why other candidates were rejected. #### World-size-one fast path The advisor should also make `num_gpus=1` an explicit serving plan, not “distributed mode with degree one everywhere.” Components should expose whether they require a process group for protocol reasons versus useful sharding. When every effective group has size one: - do not wrap the model in FSDP/sharding machinery; - do not issue rank broadcasts with no receiver; - do not construct device communicators used only by multi-rank stages; - return inputs directly from no-op collectives; and - retain only process-group state genuinely required by the server protocol. This is an execution-plan property, not a check of `dist.is_initialized()` alone. #### Suggested integration - Keep current `auto_tune.py` as the resolver/guardrail layer. - Add a separate calibration command under diffusion benchmark/profile tooling. - Store results as JSON with a schema/version and stable signature hash. - Add pipeline-config capability methods for legal degrees and topology caveats. - Add optional startup flag such as `--diffusion-parallel-plan auto:`; exact naming is open for discussion. - Expose `selected_plan`, source, rejected-plan reasons, and calibration digest in startup metrics/logs. #### Correctness tests - explicit flags always override the advisor; - illegal head/sequence/device products are rejected before launch; - exact signature match selects the recorded plan; - different candidate batch/step count does not reuse an incompatible record; - stale model/code/device revisions fail closed to a conservative path; - quality-gate failure removes a plan regardless of latency; - world-size-one plan creates no sharding wrapper or redundant broadcast; - multi-rank plans initialize every required group consistently. #### Benchmark matrix At minimum, calibrate: - logical/candidate batch `1` and one larger production-relevant batch; - CFG serial and CFG parallel where supported; - TP degrees `1/2/4` subject to legality; - one applicable SP degree for long-latent video; - cache/compile modes claimed by the final record; and - single-GPU resident execution when the model fits. Report communication time together with collective count and payload size. “Time inside all-reduce” alone does not distinguish bandwidth transfer from rank-arrival skew. #### Alternatives considered - **Static model recipes only.** Useful defaults, but cannot represent batch/shape/topology crossovers. - **Choose the widest TP that fits.** Can regress short-sequence/small-batch latency. - **Online exploration on live requests.** Risks cold compilation, OOM, and quality variation in production. - **Reconfigure topology per request.** Process-group/model-shard transitions are too expensive for phase 1; separate serving pools are safer. #### Rollout 1. Define report/signature schema and dry-run plan enumeration. 2. Add world-size-one fast-path assertions. 3. Calibrate one model across two batch regimes and publish the artifact. 4. Add startup resolver behind an explicit flag. 5. Extend model coverage only when each recommendation has end-to-end evidence. ### Related resources - SGLang Diffusion parallelism guide: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/parallelism.mdx - Current diffusion auto-tuning policy: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/server_args/auto_tune.py - Diffusion distributed state: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/parallel_state.py - Cosmos3 pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/cosmos3_pipeline.py - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py

### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Define a framework-level, side-effect-aware contract for reusing a previously computed denoising prediction on selected iterative steps while continuing to execute scheduler updates and any mandatory terminal state writes. SGLang Diffusion already integrates Cache-DiT and model-specific cache policies, but recent lifecycle bugs show that “skip a transformer call” is not a complete correctness model. Stateful world models may have several independent lifetimes at once: - request-local denoising predictions; - modality-local video and action loops; - conditional/unconditional CFG branches; and - persistent session/KV state updated only by specific real forwards. An approximate step-reuse policy can be safe only if those lifetimes and side effects are explicit. This proposal adds that contract without prescribing one universal similarity metric. #### Goals - Separate reusable denoising predictions from persistent session/KV state. - Let a model define when a real prediction is similar enough to reuse and for how many steps. - Always execute the scheduler update, even when the transformer is skipped. - Never feed reused predictions back into the similarity history as new observations. - Support independent state machines for modalities or branches with different dynamics. - Force designated real forwards when model side effects must be committed. - Make reset, CFG, distributed-decision, and failure behavior testable. #### Non-goals - Replacing Cache-DiT or standardizing one cache algorithm. - Claiming exact numerical equivalence for approximate reuse. - Reusing state across requests in phase 1. - Inferring safe terminal side effects automatically from arbitrary model code. #### Proposed contract Illustrative types: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class StepReusePolicy: policy_name: str observation_point: str # e.g. "post_cfg_velocity" history_size: int max_skip_steps: int force_real_steps: frozenset[str] # e.g. {"first_two", "terminal"} state_scope: tuple[str, ...] # request, modality, cfg_role @dataclass class StepReuseState: last_real_prediction: torch.Tensor | None = None real_history: deque[torch.Tensor] = field(default_factory=deque) skip_remaining: int = 0 real_forwards: int = 0 reused_steps: int = 0 @dataclass(frozen=True) class StepSideEffectContract: terminal_write_required: bool = False write_tags: frozenset[str] = frozenset() ``` The model adapter supplies `observe_real_prediction(...)`, `decide_reuse(...)`, and side-effect metadata. The runtime supplies lifecycle, isolation, metrics, and distributed agreement. #### Execution flow ```mermaid flowchart TD Start["Begin request / modality loop
fresh StepReuseState"] Step["Next denoising step"] Force{"Real forward required?
warmup, no history, terminal side effect"} Budget{"skip_remaining > 0?"} Real["Run transformer"] Observe["Apply CFG, then record
real prediction only"] Decide["Model policy computes
bounded reuse budget"] Reuse["Reuse last real prediction"] Sched["Always run scheduler update"] More{"More steps?"} Finalize["Verify mandatory writes
and emit metrics"] Start --> Step --> Force Force -->|yes| Real --> Observe --> Decide --> Sched Force -->|no| Budget Budget -->|yes| Reuse --> Sched Budget -->|no| Real Sched --> More More -->|yes| Step More -->|no| Finalize ``` #### Lifecycle and isolation rules 1. State is created per logical request and per declared scope. Video and action loops do not share history unless a model explicitly declares that safe. 2. The first observations are real. A policy cannot make a similarity decision from reused values. 3. Reused predictions never enter `real_history`. 4. The scheduler advances on every configured step. 5. Terminal real-forward requirements override every reuse budget. 6. A request error, cancellation, reset, or session change destroys request-local reuse state. 7. Reuse is disabled by default and invalid policy parameters fail at configuration/admission time. #### CFG and distributed semantics The observation point must be explicit. For common two-branch CFG, a policy that compares the final guided velocity should observe *after* the conditional/unconditional merge. A policy that operates per branch must declare two independent states. All ranks participating in TP/SP/CFG parallelism must take the same execute/reuse decision. Phase 1 should compute the decision on the stage's control rank and broadcast a compact decision token, or derive it from replicated tensors proven identical. Rank-local threshold decisions are not safe because a one-ULP difference near a threshold can desynchronize collective control flow. The current Cache-DiT lifecycle issue involving serial CFG and CFG parallel is relevant evidence that reset ownership must be stated once and shared by every execution mode rather than inferred from wrapper placement. #### Integration proposal - Add a small `StepReuseController` adjacent to, not inside, the generic denoising loop. - Let existing Cache-DiT adapters remain unchanged initially. - Expose lifecycle hooks: `begin_scope`, `before_step`, `after_real_forward`, `after_scheduler_step`, and `finalize_scope`. - Add model adapters only for architectures with an explicit observation point and quality evaluation. - Keep persistent session/KV updates in model state; the controller merely enforces declared mandatory real-forward points. For LingBot-style world-action models, one adapter could create separate video and action scopes, compare FP32 post-CFG velocities, and declare a terminal real forward needed to install persistent rollout state. The framework should not embed those model-specific thresholds. #### Correctness and quality gates Required unit tests: - first `history_size` observations are real; - skip countdown is bounded and cannot underflow; - only real predictions update history; - scheduler is called for every step; - terminal write is forced after a long reuse streak; - state is isolated across requests, modalities, CFG roles, and retries; - invalid thresholds/history/budgets fail closed; - all distributed ranks receive the same decision token; - serial CFG and CFG-parallel lifecycle produces the same reset count. Required end-to-end validation: - cache off vs on with fixed seeds; - per-step real/reused trace; - public output quality metric plus internal trajectory metrics; - persistent state/KV equality after the forced terminal write where exact equality is expected; - multiple schedules and request lengths, not only one single-step sample. #### Observability Per request and per scope: - possible, real, and reused transformer forwards; - reuse streak lengths; - similarity/decision statistics (sampled or debug-only); - forced-real reason; - scheduler steps executed; - terminal-write verification result; and - fallback/disable reason. #### Alternatives considered - **A model-local boolean cache.** It cannot express independent modalities, terminal writes, or distributed decision agreement. - **Use only Cache-DiT wrapper state.** Existing algorithms remain useful, but wrapper placement alone does not define side effects and lifecycle for stateful world models. - **Skip scheduler steps together with transformer steps.** This changes the solver trajectory and is out of scope. - **Compare reused predictions recursively.** That makes self-reuse look artificially stable and can extend skipping without new evidence. #### Rollout 1. Land contract/controller tests with a synthetic iterative model. 2. Add trace-only mode that computes decisions but executes every real forward. 3. Validate one opt-in model adapter against full trajectory and public output gates. 4. Enable explicit opt-in configuration; keep defaults unchanged. 5. Generalize only after serial CFG, CFG-parallel, and session-state cases pass. ### Related resources - SGLang Diffusion denoising and Cache-DiT integration: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - Cache-DiT documentation: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/cache_dit.mdx - LingBot-World causal pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/lingbot_world_causal_dmd_pipeline.py - Related CFG lifecycle bug: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/35054 - Related exact dependency-aware reuse RFC in vLLM-Omni (different reuse class): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/6238

items.title: [Feature] Batched Candidate-Trajectory Ensembling for Stochastic Action Generation
items.body:
### Checklist - [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Motivation #### Summary Add a first-class, opt-in execution contract for generating multiple independent action trajectories from one conditioning context, executing the candidates as one physical batch, and reducing them to one served action result. SGLang Diffusion already has most of the lower-level pieces: - `Req.num_outputs_per_prompt` represents multiple outputs; - latent preparation preserves per-request RNG streams and batches the deterministic packing/scaling work; - pipeline stages can expand shared conditioning to the sample batch; and - Cosmos3 is implemented as a composed pipeline with explicit latent, timestep, denoising, action, and decode stages. What is missing is a model/runtime contract that says these outputs are *candidates for one logical prediction*, not independent public media outputs. Without that distinction, a world-action model has to implement sequential sampling or ad hoc aggregation inside model code, and the runtime cannot preserve candidate identity, enforce RNG independence, or measure the benefit of batching. This proposal is intentionally narrow. It does not propose averaging images or videos, and it does not change default `num_outputs_per_prompt` behavior. It adds an opt-in path for models whose public action output has a validated candidate reducer. #### Proposed execution contract Illustrative types: ```python @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateTrajectorySpec: count: int = 1 reducer: str = "none" # "none", "mean", or a registered model reducer return_candidates: bool = False seed_policy: str = "per_candidate" @dataclass(frozen=True) class CandidateGroup: request_id: str candidate_ids: tuple[int, ...] public_output: str = "action" ``` The model/pipeline adapter would declare: 1. which tensor is the candidate action trajectory; 2. whether reduction occurs before or after denormalization; 3. the supported reducer and output dtype/shape; 4. which conditioning tensors are candidate-invariant; and 5. whether video or another auxiliary branch must execute for action correctness. The runtime owns grouping, candidate identity, batching, failure handling, observability, and final response construction. The model owns the mathematical reduction rule. #### Request and execution flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Req["One logical request
conditioning + candidate count N"] Validate["Validate model capability
and candidate contract"] Seeds["Create N independent
request-owned RNG streams"] Shared["Compute candidate-invariant
conditioning once"] Expand["Expand/fan out conditioning
and build candidate batch"] Denoise["One batched denoising path
candidate axis = N"] Action["Model-specific action
postprocessing"] Reduce["Validated reducer
mean or registered reducer"] Resp["One public action result
optional raw candidates"] Req --> Validate --> Seeds --> Shared --> Expand --> Denoise --> Action --> Reduce --> Resp ``` #### RNG and equivalence rules Candidate batching must not collapse stochastic independence or silently change seed semantics. - Candidate `i` receives a stable stream derived from `(base_seed, i)` or an explicitly supplied generator. - `count=1` must preserve the current output exactly. - For a fixed candidate seed list, batched execution must produce the same candidate set as the sequential reference under the model's declared equivalence rule. - Candidate ordering is stable across dynamic batching and output slicing. - Retry/fallback may rerun the whole group, but must not reuse a partially advanced generator as though it were fresh. The existing grouped latent-preparation logic is a useful precedent: it already draws request-owned random latents separately and only batches deterministic work afterward. The candidate path should retain the same property. #### Scheduler and batching behavior Phase 1 should admit a candidate group atomically when it fits the configured execution batch. If it does not fit, the runtime should fail clearly or use a documented sequential fallback; it should not silently truncate the group. A later phase may split candidates into microbatches and aggregate when all slices finish, but the request state must then track: - candidate IDs completed/pending; - seed/generator state per candidate; - partial reducer state; and - cancellation semantics for the entire logical request. Candidate-invariant conditioning should be encoded once where the stage contract permits it. An adapter may use an expanded view or an explicit attention fan-out; physical tensor replication is not required by this RFC. #### Integration points Suggested initial ownership: - request fields and validation: diffusion sampling/request data; - group identity and completion: request/scheduler state; - independent raw noise: `LatentPreparationStage`; - conditioning expansion: pipeline configuration's existing sample-batch expansion hook; - candidate reducer: a small action-output capability implemented by opt-in world-model pipelines; - metrics: candidate count, physical forwards, fallback reason, reducer time, and action-only branch time. The first model integration could be Cosmos3 action generation because SGLang already has an explicit Cosmos3 composed pipeline. The framework abstraction should not contain Cosmos-specific tensor names. #### Correctness and quality gates Required tests: 1. `count=1` is identical to the existing path. 2. Fixed per-candidate seeds produce the same ordered candidate tensors in sequential and batched modes. 3. The reduced action matches a standalone reducer applied to captured candidate tensors. 4. Candidate IDs remain stable when unrelated requests are co-batched. 5. CFG serial and CFG-parallel paths preserve candidate membership. 6. TP/SP output reconstruction happens before reduction when the action tensor is sharded. 7. Cancellation and one-candidate failure do not return a partial aggregate as a valid result. 8. Auxiliary video decode can be skipped only when the model declares it irrelevant to the action output. Quality validation must be model-specific. The framework should report candidate-level and reduced-output artifacts but should not hard-code a universal action metric or assume that a larger candidate count always improves quality. #### Benchmark plan Report, for `N in {1, 2, 4, 8, 10}`: - sequential reference latency; - batched latency and peak memory; - number of physical transformer forwards; - conditioning encode time; - candidate-reduction time; - candidate tensor parity under fixed seeds; and - model-declared action-quality metrics. Benchmark at more than one parallel topology. Wider TP may help the larger candidate batch while regressing `N=1`; the RFC should not encode one topology as universally optimal. #### Alternatives considered - **Keep aggregation in application code.** This forces repeated RPCs or model-specific server loops and prevents the runtime from preserving one logical request/candidate group. - **Treat candidates as ordinary independent outputs.** This loses the reduction contract and makes failure/cancellation semantics ambiguous. - **Always expose raw candidates.** This moves a model-system accuracy feature into every client and expands the public payload unnecessarily. - **Average videos/latents generically.** Out of scope and not semantically valid for this proposal. #### Rollout 1. Land internal types and validation with no model enabled. 2. Add a Cosmos3 action adapter and sequential-equivalence tests. 3. Add atomic candidate-group scheduling and metrics. 4. Benchmark before enabling any default. 5. Consider microbatching and additional reducers only after the initial contract is stable. ### Related resources - Cosmos3 composed pipeline: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines/cosmos3_pipeline.py - Latent preparation and per-request RNG handling: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/latent_preparation.py - Diffusion denoising stage and sample-batch expansion: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/denoising.py - vLLM-Omni request-selected output routing RFC (complementary output-branch contract): https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/6302

items.title: [Bug] DSA top-k v2: tie-overflow selection is not exact — silently returns wrong top-k members (follow-up to #30512 / #30645)
items.body:
## Summary

PR #30512 and #30645 fixed the *crash/validity* symptoms of threshold-bin tie
overflow in the fused DSA top-k v2 kernel (all output slots written, no `-1`
inside the valid prefix, inf-boundary handling). However the *exactness* gap
remains, on `main` as of `ea27e3d`: when more than `kMaxNumTie = 2048`
elements fall into the threshold coarse bin, the collect pass keeps whichever
2048 arrive first (`atomicAdd` order — scheduling-dependent, value-independent)
and the exact tie-break then runs on that arbitrary subset:

```cpp
// topk_impl.cuh (main @ ea27e3d, L595 / L618; same in v0.5.15–v0.5.17)
const auto count_eq = atomicAdd(&smem->count_eq, 1);
if (count_eq < kMaxNumTie) [[likely]]
  smem->tie.values[count_eq] = {val, idx};       // overflow: value silently dropped
...
const auto tie_count = min(equal_count, kMaxNumTie);  // select from truncated subset
```

Elements in one coarse bin share only the top fp16 bits — they are *not*
fp32-equal — so the dropped candidates can be genuinely larger than the kept
ones. The kernel then returns indices that are not the true top-k, with no
error or flag, and sparse attention reads wrong KV positions. Note
`count_eq` already holds the true bin population, so the overflow is
detectable for free; it is just not acted on.

This is distinct from the ReLU-degenerate exact-tie case discussed in #30645
(thousands of positions on one exact value — there any subset is acceptable).
Our comparison below is against the `torch.topk` **fp32 score multiset**, i.e.
exact ties with different indices are accepted; the mismatches are real value
losses.

## Evidence on real workloads

GLM-5.2-FP8, 8xB200 TP8, official v0.5.17 image, ~1M-token contexts. We dumped
real indexer score rows (~21 top-k layers x 2 adjacent decode steps = 42 rows
per workload) and compared kernel output to `torch.topk` fp32 multisets:

| workload (1M ctx, batch=1) | rows not exact |
|---|---|
| real model logits (synthetic prompt) | 3 / 42 |
| SGLang source-code corpus | 2 / 42 |
| Gutenberg novels corpus | 2 / 42 |

Additional data points:

- Measured threshold-band candidate populations on these rows reach
  **4.7k–31k** vs the 2048 buffer; on the worst rows the output missed
  **1084–1591 of 2048** true top-k members (measured on the same mechanism in
  the v0.5.15 era).
- In a 32K–1M x batch 1–32 microbench matrix, 9 of 21 cells were not exact on
  at least one of five real-score inputs (64K–512K, batch 2–8 included).
- #30512's own device-side diagnostic corroborates trigger frequency: 41
  overflowing rows within a ~9-minute GLM-5.2 bench (`equal_count` up to 1536
  vs the then-1024 cap).

## Reproduction

### A. Suggested minimal repro (synthetic, no model)

Sketch adapted from our validation harness — construct one row where >2048
fp32-distinct values share one fp16 coarse bin:

```python
import torch
from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.topk import plan_topk_v2, topk_transform_512_v2

N, TOPK, PAGE = 262_144, 2048, 64
dev = "cuda"

scores = torch.full((1, N), -100.0, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
n_narrow = 50_000   # 50k distinct values inside one fp16 bucket
scores[0, :n_narrow] = 1.0 + torch.arange(n_narrow, device=dev, dtype=torch.float32) * 1e-9

seq_lens = torch.tensor([N], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
page_table = torch.arange((N + PAGE - 1) // PAGE, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).unsqueeze(0)
out = torch.full((1, TOPK), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)

plan = plan_topk_v2(seq_lens)
topk_transform_512_v2(scores, seq_lens, page_table, out, PAGE, plan)

ref_idx = torch.topk(scores[0], TOPK).indices
ref_phys = page_table[0, ref_idx // PAGE] * PAGE + ref_idx % PAGE
missing = set(ref_phys.tolist()) - set(out[0].tolist())
print(f"true top-k members missing from kernel output: {len(missing)} / {TOPK}")
```

The true top-2048 are the *last* 2048 of the narrow band; arrival order keeps
an arbitrary subset, so `missing > 0` whenever the overflow path is taken.
(Post-#30512/#30645 the output contains valid indices — the failure is purely
exactness.) We will follow up with the exact numbers from a fresh run of this
script on B200.

### B. Real rows

We can share the dumped 1M score rows and the multiset-comparison harness used
for the table above on request.

## Suggested fix

1. **Minimal**: after collect, if `count_eq > kMaxNumTie`, take a slow path
   instead of proceeding on the truncated subset. The counter already exists;
   non-overflowing rows pay nothing.
2. **Complete**: progressive refinement — on overflow, subdivide the threshold
   bin by the next bits of the order-preserving fp32 key (12→10→10 covers all
   32 bits) until the candidate set fits; at full depth, remaining ties are
   exactly equal fp32 values and any subset is correct. We run this scheme in a
   production-shaped kernel: 126/126 real rows exact on the three workloads
   above; the refinement branch is rarely taken so the common path is
   unaffected.

A narrow-distribution regression test (shape of Repro A) in
`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_v2.py` would prevent
reintroduction.

items.title: [Bug] PrefillDelayer can enter a persistent mixed-state feedback loop and collapse prefill progress under DP Attention + chunked prefill
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues / PRs and did not find one matching this exact failure mode.
- [x] The issue is reproducible across repeated runs with the same server/client configuration.
- [x] Requests complete successfully; this is primarily a scheduler / performance-stability issue rather than a model-correctness failure.
- [x] I compared the behavior against `PrefillDelayer` disabled and inspected the relevant scheduler / delayer source code.
- [x] I collected per-DP-rank scheduler metrics and prefill-progress counters.

---

## Summary

Under a long-prefill workload with:

- DeepSeek-V4-Pro
- TP=8
- DP=8
- DP Attention enabled
- chunked prefill enabled
- PrefillDelayer enabled
- one 8-GPU node

an identical server configuration and deterministic workload can enter two qualitatively different runtime regimes:

### Healthy synchronized state

- Input throughput: ~94.6–94.8k tok/s
- DP ranks progress through prefill nearly in lockstep
- `PrefillDelayer` converges to sustained `all / no_wait`
- average running requests is ~8.5

### Pathological LOW state

- Input throughput: ~62–79k tok/s
- within the first ~5 s of the formal workload, DP-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer number of effective prefill chunks
- the first observed spread is typically exactly **16384 tokens**, i.e. one effective per-rank chunk
- `PrefillDelayer` remains dominated by `mixed / delay`
- average running requests collapses to ~0.15
- residual / under-filled prefill batches increase sharply

This is not explained by persistent per-rank request-count imbalance. In one representative LOW run, the first 30 s admitted exactly the same number of sequences on all 8 DP ranks, yet rank-level prefill progress had already diverged by one full chunk within 5 s.

Disabling `PrefillDelayer` does **not** recover the healthy state. Instead, the system enters a third regime with lower but more continuous concurrency:

- throughput: ~48–68k tok/s
- avg running requests: ~4.7–5.9
- residual batches: ~11–14%

Therefore the LOW state with PrefillDelayer enabled is not equivalent to "PrefillDelayer disabled". It appears to be a distinct scheduler regime in which the delayer participates in suppressing prefill progress.

The exact upstream trigger is still being localized. I am opening this issue because the observed `mixed/delay` feedback loop appears different from the already-known `all/slot_condition` starvation fixed in #29898.

---

## Environment

```text
SGLang version : 0.5.14
commit         : 49e384ce9d304648e9959666ecb8ce8cd98d0deb
git log -1     : 49e384c [Cherry-pick to release/v0.5.14] Revert Gemma4 modelopt fp4 MoE backend change (#28347) (#29246)
git describe   : v0.5.14
remote         : https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang.git
local patches  : no tracked-file modifications
```

The earlier scheduler-debug instrumentation was fully reverted before the measurements described here. The remaining untracked files were only local backup files / an empty accidental file; tracked scheduler source matched the clean release tree.

Hardware / topology:

```text
1 node
8 × NVIDIA B30Z
TP = 8
DP = 8
DP Attention = enabled
MoE A2A backend = MegaMoE
```

Relevant server configuration:

```bash
--tp 8
--dp 8
--enable-dp-attention
--enable-prefill-delayer
--chunked-prefill-size 131072
```

With DP Attention, the effective per-rank prefill chunk is:

```text
131072 / 8 = 16384 tokens
```

Relevant MegaMoE cap:

```bash
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16512
```

Workload:

```text
input length    : 60000
output length   : 1
max concurrency : 16
num prompts     : 160
ignore_eos      : true
seed            : 1
```

The 60k prompt is therefore processed approximately as:

```text
16384 + 16384 + 16384 + remainder
```

The client workload is burst-style; no request-rate throttling or intentional staggering is used in the baseline.

---

## Reproduction behavior

Representative post-reboot runs:

| Run | Input TPS | Median TTFT | avg running | avg queue | residual batches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 94,634 | 9.66 s | 8.13 | 0.16 | 11.96% |
| LOW | 72,923 | 12.38 s | 0.17 | 0.84 | 27.17% |
| LOW | 62,379 | 13.81 s | 0.12 | 0.85 | 29.03% |
| good | 94,690 | 9.65 s | 8.37 | 0.17 | 9.52% |
| mid | 82,688 | 9.68 s | 5.90 | 0.29 | 12.81% |
| LOW | 78,571 | 10.45 s | 0.24 | 0.84 | 28.41% |

The healthy-state throughput is extremely stable (~94.6k tok/s, sub-percent variation), while LOW runs have a qualitatively different scheduler signature rather than ordinary run-to-run noise.

A host reboot did not eliminate the problem.

---

## Observation 1: LOW starts as a rank-level prefill-progress divergence

Using the per-rank counter:

```text
sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank="...", mode="prefill_compute"}
```

I computed:

```text
progress_spread(t) = max_i(prefill_tokens_i(t)) - min_i(prefill_tokens_i(t))
```

Results:

| Run | TPS | spread@5s | spread@10s | spread@15s | spread@20s | spread@30s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 94,634 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| good | 94,690 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| mid | 82,688 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| LOW | 72,923 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 11k | 16k |
| LOW | 62,379 | 16k | 16k | 60k | 60k | 60k |
| LOW | 78,571 | 16k | 22k | 27k | 0 | 0 |

The important feature is that the first LOW-state divergence is quantized at approximately:

```text
16384 tokens
```

which is exactly one effective prefill chunk.

`realtime_tokens_total` is incremented from `report_prefill_stats()` after a prefill batch result is processed, so this metric represents completed/reported prefill progress. It does **not** by itself prove whether the original cause was scheduler suppression or slower GPU execution.

### Metric-cadence validation

I separately validated the observable cadence of `realtime_tokens_total` using 0.2 s scrapes during a smaller N32/C16 run with the same 16k effective chunk.

Across all ranks:

```text
jump interval p50 = 1.397 s
jump interval p95 = 1.535 s
min interval       = 0.401 s
```

Jump-size distribution:

```text
16384 ×112   (one full chunk)
11264 ×8     (tail chunks)
256   ×3     (small startup fragments)
32768 ×0     (no two-chunk merge observed)
```

Thus the progress-spread observation is not an artifact of multiple 16k completions being collapsed into one scrape sample in this validation run.

---

## Observation 2: persistent request-count imbalance is not required for LOW

I counted per-rank `#new-seq` admissions during the first 30 s of the formal workload.

| Run | r0 | r1 | r2 | r3 | r4 | r5 | r6 | r7 | range | CV |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| good | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 27 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% |
| good | 26 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 25 | 26 | 1 | 1.8% |
| mid | 27 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 26 | 1 | 1.4% |
| LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | **0** | **0.0%** |
| LOW | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 | 17 | 18 | 18 | 1 | 2.6% |
| LOW | 14 | 15 | 10 | 14 | 10 | 14 | 13 | 14 | 5 | 14.8% |

The strongest case is the 72.9k TPS LOW run:

```text
18 18 18 18 18 18 18 18
```

All eight ranks admitted exactly the same number of sequences during the first 30 s, yet prefill progress had already diverged by one 16k chunk at 5 s.

Therefore persistent per-rank request-count imbalance is not a necessary condition for entering the LOW state.

Sub-second request-arrival / dispatch timing skew is **not** ruled out by this measurement. Also, `#new-seq` is scheduler admission into a prefill batch, not a direct counter of the initial DataParallelController request dispatch.

---

## Observation 3: PrefillDelayer state strongly separates healthy and LOW runs

From:

```text
sglang:prefill_delayer_outcomes_total
```

healthy runs eventually converge to sustained:

```text
input_estimation="all"
output_reason="no_wait"
```

while LOW runs remain dominated by:

```text
input_estimation="mixed"
output_reason="delay"
```

In healthy runs, after an initial transient, `mixed/delay` can disappear for long intervals and all 8 ranks repeatedly observe an immediately releasable state.

In LOW runs, `mixed/delay` remains persistent and the scheduler never establishes the same synchronized regime.

I use:

```text
all_no_wait / (all_no_wait + mixed_delay)
```

only as a diagnostic state index, not as a literal request-release probability, because `mixed/delay` may be counted repeatedly across multiple scheduler passes during one waiting episode.

The observed behavior is best described as synchronization / phase-locking-like behavior; I am not claiming a formal oscillator model.

---

## Observation 4: LOW is not equivalent to disabling PrefillDelayer

I ran a separate six-run experiment with the same 16k effective chunk but with PrefillDelayer disabled.

| Run | Input TPS | avg running | residual batches | median TTFT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 67,658 | 5.65 | 11.78% | 12.62 s |
| 2 | 48,536 | 4.73 | 12.01% | 15.11 s |
| 3 | 53,299 | 5.26 | 11.18% | 15.43 s |
| 4 | 64,174 | 5.36 | 12.24% | 13.29 s |
| 5 | 55,500 | 4.69 | 14.04% | 15.70 s |
| 6 | 64,715 | 5.90 | 12.02% | 13.10 s |

Mean throughput:

```text
58,980 tok/s
CV = 12.88%
```

The important mechanism difference is:

```text
PrefillDelayer ON, healthy : avg running ≈ 8.5
PrefillDelayer ON, deep LOW: avg running ≈ 0.15
PrefillDelayer OFF         : avg running ≈ 4.7–5.9
```

Thus the ON-LOW state is not simply the delayer becoming ineffective and behaving like OFF. The delayer-enabled LOW regime suppresses running concurrency far more aggressively than the OFF regime.

This OFF experiment was not interleaved with the ON runs, so I do **not** use it to estimate relative state-entry probabilities. I also do not claim six samples prove a statistically unimodal OFF distribution. The robust observation is the mechanism-signature difference above.

---

## Observation 5: staggered arrivals make the failure worse

As a diagnostic experiment, I changed the formal client traffic from a burst to:

```text
2 requests/s, fixed interval
```

while keeping concurrency=16.

This was intentionally stopped after the direction was clearly harmful.

Representative results:

```text
burst: 94,630 tok/s
ramp : 53,449 tok/s

burst: 64,016 tok/s
ramp : LOW again
```

The ramp sends approximately one new request every 0.5 s. With DP=8 this naturally exposes only a subset of ranks to new work at a time, increasing the probability that the delayer observes a `mixed` state.

This is not presented as a production benchmark because the arrival process itself changed. It is included because the behavior is consistent with the delayer being highly sensitive to cross-rank arrival phase.

Related newer work such as #35191 independently discusses trickle arrivals and persistent fragmented prefills, although that PR operates on a newer optional queue-trigger path that is not enabled in this configuration.

---

## Local source comparison against later upstream fixes

I compared this exact `v0.5.14` tree against several later PrefillDelayer / scheduler fixes.

### 1. #29898 — missing locally

The local `PrefillDelayer` has a bounded delay in the `mixed` branch:

```python
prev_delayed_count = prev_state.delayed_count if prev_state else 0
if prev_delayed_count < self._max_delay_passes - 1:
    ...
    output_reason="delay"
else:
    ...
    output_reason="wait_timeout"
```

but its `all` branch can still delay indefinitely when `slot_condition` or `queue_condition` remains true:

```python
if slot_condition or queue_condition:
    ...
    next_state = next_state.bump_delayed_count()
    return _NegotiateOutput(
        output_allow=False,
        output_reason="delay",
        ...
    )
```

with no equivalent `max_delay_passes` bound.

This confirms that the local tree predates #29898.

However, I do **not** claim #29898 is the direct cause here: in the collected workload, `all/delay` was not observed; the pathological state is dominated by `mixed/delay`.

Its relevance is that upstream has independently confirmed that PrefillDelayer feedback can cause prefill starvation and running-batch collapse.

---

### 2. #31835 — current reproduction hits the older negotiation placement

The local `schedule_policy.py` contains two paths:

```text
add_one_req_ignore_eos()  -> negotiation after budget/admission checks
add_one_req()             -> negotiation at the beginning of the function
```

The dispatch condition is:

```python
if req.sampling_params.ignore_eos and getattr(self.tree_cache, "disable", True):
    return self.add_one_req_ignore_eos(req)
```

This reproduction has:

```text
ignore_eos = true
radix cache enabled -> tree_cache.disable = false
```

so the condition is false and the workload falls through to `add_one_req()`.

In the local tree, `add_one_req()` begins with:

```python
if (self.prefill_delayer_single_pass is not None) and (
    not self.prefill_delayer_single_pass.negotiate_should_allow_prefill(
        local_prefillable=True,
        running_batch=self.running_batch.batch_size(),
        max_prefill_bs=self.max_prefill_bs,
        max_running_requests=self.max_running_requests,
        waiting_queue_len=self.waiting_queue_len,
    )
):
    return AddReqResult.OTHER
```

before later request / chunk / admission checks.

Therefore, on the actual reproduction path, `local_prefillable=True` is sampled before all subsequent admission checks. The alternate `add_one_req_ignore_eos()` path samples after budget checks, so the two paths have different semantics.

This is directly relevant to interpretation of `all/mixed`: `local_prefillable` is a scheduler-side estimate whose meaning depends on where it is sampled, not a direct GPU-readiness signal.

That said, I do **not** currently think this semantic issue alone explains the LOW state. In the failing workload, KV/SWA pressure is very low (observed full-pool usage ~0.55%, SWA usage ~2.74%), so most post-negotiation admission checks are unlikely to fail. The placement issue is therefore real in this path but not yet demonstrated to be the active trigger.

---

### 3. #30295 — key chunked-request double-count shape is still present

The local scheduler already contains an early guard:

```python
if (
    self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs) <= 0
    and self.chunked_req is None
    ...
):
```

but the later waiting-queue loop still contains:

```python
if len(adder.can_run_list) >= self.get_num_allocatable_reqs(running_bs):
    self.running_batch.batch_is_full = True
```

while `add_chunked_req(...)` adds the in-flight chunked request to `self.can_run_list`, and `get_num_allocatable_reqs()` uses:

```python
min(
    pp_max_micro_batch_size - running_bs,
    req_to_token_pool.available_size(),
)
```

where the in-flight request's slot is already reflected in `available_size()`.

This preserves the shape of the later double-count fixed by #30295.

I do not think this alone explains the reported collapse: #30295 causes a stable one-slot loss, whereas the LOW state here collapses avg running from approximately 8.5 to approximately 0.15. It may still be an adjacent bug or amplification factor.

---

### 4. #24768 — present locally, but current configuration uses CPU/Gloo negotiation

The local tree contains the NCCL/device-group option for PrefillDelayer synchronization.

With the current settings:

```text
disable_overlap_schedule = false
SGLANG_NCCL_ALL_GATHER_IN_OVERLAP_SCHEDULER_SYNC_BATCH = false
```

PrefillDelayer uses the CPU/Gloo negotiation path.

Enabling the NCCL synchronization path in this MegaMoE configuration was not stable in my environment and led to an NVLink/barrier timeout, so it is not currently usable as a workaround.

If the failure is ultimately localized to scheduler/readiness coordination, this cross-DP negotiation path is one area I plan to investigate further.

---

### 5. #35191 — not directly active, but relevant to the dynamics

This newer work describes a separate PrefillDelayer problem where trickle arrivals can keep the observed batching target small and sustain fragmented prefills.

The optional queue-trigger feature involved there is not enabled in this workload (`queue_min_ratio` unset), so this is not a direct code-path match.

It is nevertheless consistent with the observation here that staggered arrivals strongly destabilize synchronized prefill behavior.

---

## Current interpretation

The strongest evidence currently supports this descriptive sequence:

```text
formal workload begins
        ↓
DP ranks initially receive approximately balanced request counts
        ↓
within the first few seconds,
per-rank prefill progress diverges by an integer prefill-chunk amount
        ↓
PrefillDelayer repeatedly observes mixed states
        ↓
mixed/delay persists
        ↓
under-filled / residual batches increase
        ↓
running concurrency collapses
        ↓
LOW throughput state becomes self-sustaining
```

One causal distinction is still unresolved:

### Hypothesis B — execution-duration divergence

One or more ranks receive comparable forward work but their GPU forward takes longer:

```text
same/similar forward opportunity
        ↓
one rank completes later
        ↓
prefill progress diverges
        ↓
Delayer subsequently observes mixed
```

### Hypothesis C — scheduler/readiness suppression

The scheduler / delayer gives some ranks fewer forward opportunities:

```text
scheduler readiness / negotiation diverges
        ↓
Delayer suppresses some prefill admissions
        ↓
those ranks do less forward work
        ↓
prefill progress diverges
```

I am instrumenting:

```text
sglang:realtime_tokens_total{dp_rank,mode="prefill_compute"}
```

together with:

```text
sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total{dp_rank,category}
```

using `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`.

The DeviceTimer implementation uses CUDA events plus non-blocking `end_event.query()` rather than `synchronize()`, but I am first validating that enabling the timer itself does not perturb this timing-sensitive synchronization state.

The intended discriminator is **not** event timestamp ordering, because Delayer negotiation necessarily precedes forward completion in the source code. Instead, the discriminator is the per-rank relationship between:

```text
Δprefill_progress
and
Δcompleted_forward_execution_time
```

over a short window after the first rank-level progress divergence.

Roughly:

```text
ΔP lower and ΔF proportionally lower
→ rank likely completed less forward work
→ supports scheduler/readiness-side cause

ΔP lower but ΔF similar or higher
→ rank spent comparable/more GPU time for less progress
→ supports execution-duration-side cause
```

This follow-up work is ongoing and is not required for the observations reported above.

---

## Why I think this deserves a separate issue

I could not find an upstream issue matching all of these properties together:

```text
DP Attention
+ PrefillDelayer
+ chunked long-prefill workload
+ same deterministic configuration
+ healthy ~94.8k state vs persistent LOW state
+ LOW dominated by mixed/delay
+ avg running collapsing near zero
+ rank progress diverging by exactly one effective prefill chunk
+ request-count admission remaining balanced in at least one LOW reproduction
```

#29898 is the closest known failure family, but it is specifically an `all / slot_condition` liveness bug.

The behavior reported here appears to be a different `mixed`-branch feedback failure mode.

---

## Questions for maintainers

1. Is a persistent `mixed/delay` loop with very low `num_running_reqs` an expected / known failure mode of PrefillDelayer?

2. Are there known cases where the cross-DP `local_prefillable` negotiation can remain phase-shifted even when request counts are balanced across DP ranks?

3. Is there a known interaction between chunked prefill, an in-flight `chunked_req`, `can_run_list`, `batch_is_full`, and PrefillDelayer state that can create a self-reinforcing mixed state?

4. Would you expect #29898 / #31835 / #30295 to materially change this workload even though the observed state is primarily `mixed/delay` rather than `all/delay`?

5. Is there a recommended way to trace the first divergence between per-rank PrefillDelayer negotiation, prefill admission, and model-forward execution without materially perturbing scheduler timing?

---

## Additional data available

I retained:

- per-run server logs
- per-rank Prefill batch logs
- `#new-seq` / `#new-token` traces
- 0.2 s Prometheus cadence captures
- per-rank `realtime_tokens_total`
- PrefillDelayer outcome counters
- queue/running-request counters
- host/GPU telemetry
- good-state and LOW-state profiling artifacts

I can provide a reduced reproduction package or additional per-rank timelines if useful.

items.title: [Bug] NIXL/UCX prefill segfault (nixlUcxSharedThread -> cuEventQuery) is not fixed — reproduces on v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200; #23489 and #23499 were closed without a root cause
items.body:
## Summary

The NIXL/UCX prefill segfault reported in #23489 and #23499 is **not fixed**. Both issues were
closed without a root cause — #23489 same-day as "Resolved via rebase", #23499 with no linked PR or
commit — and #23499 already has an unanswered 2026-07-07 comment from someone hitting it again on a
different GPU/CUDA/SGLang combination.

We reproduce it today on **v0.5.17 / CUDA 13.0 / B200 x86**, and we have traced it to a missing
CUDA context in NIXL's UCX progress thread. Filing separately here because SGLang's
`num_threads = 8` choice for prefill is what exposes every NIXL PD user to it, while decode's `0`
makes decode immune.

Upstream issue: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/2102

## Reproduction

Production 8×B200 host, both roles co-located:

- prefill: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 0-3, decode: TP4/DP4 on GPUs 4-7
- `--disaggregation-transfer-backend nixl`, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`
- `nixl` / `nixl-cu13` 1.3.2, `UCX_TLS=cuda_copy,cuda_ipc,tcp`, `UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n`
- image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.17-cu130`

**9 prefill crashes in 43 hours** of steady traffic, ~one every 4.8h, evenly spread across the
clock — not tied to load, deploys, or any request shape. The decode role, on the same host with the
same image, UCX env and traffic, has **never** crashed.

## Stack — identical every time

```
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

  File "<unknown>", line 0, in cuEventQuery
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in uct_cuda_base_iface_event_fd_arm
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in ucp_worker_arm
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxWorker::arm() const
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in nixlUcxSharedThread::run()
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in __clone
```

## A debugging note that cost us time

`faulthandler` dumps **every** thread, and the Python main-thread frame is different on every
crash — we saw `deepseek_v4_backend.init_compression_metadata`, `mem_cache/allocator/swa.free_swa`,
`forward_batch_info.init_new`, `scheduler_components/dp_attn.all_gather`, and
`utils/common.broadcast_pyobj` across nine dumps of the same bug. All of those are innocent
bystanders. Only the C++ frames matter, and they never change.

Likewise the `Scheduler hit an exception: ... RuntimeError: [gloo] ... Connection reset by peer`
tracebacks that follow are the surviving DP ranks reacting to a dead peer, not the fault. #23499's
original report made the same observation.

Anyone triaging a report like this should grep the dump for `nixlUcxSharedThread`, not for the
scheduler frames.

## Root cause

`nixlUcxSharedThread::run()` (nixl `src/plugins/ucx/ucx_backend.cpp:339`) calls `worker->arm()`
without ever establishing a CUDA context on that thread. `arm()` reaches UCX's `cuda_copy`
transport, which calls `cuEventQuery` and segfaults. NIXL's UCX plugin contains **no** CUDA context
management at all — a repo-wide grep for `vramApplyCtx|pthrCudaCtx|cuCtxSetCurrent` hits only
`src/plugins/libfabric/`, which received exactly this fix in ai-dynamo/nixl#1157.

## Why prefill only

`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`:

```python
num_threads = 8 if disaggregation_mode == DisaggregationMode.PREFILL else 0
```

and in nixl `ucx_backend.cpp:763`, the shared progress thread is only constructed when the UCX
backend receives `num_threads > 0`. So prefill gets `nixlUcxSharedThread` and decode does not,
which matches our 9-vs-0 crash split exactly.

## Workaround (confirmed at the source level, running it now)

```bash
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS='{"num_threads":"0"}'
```

The `setdefault` in `conn.py` means an explicit value wins, and `num_threads=0` makes NIXL skip
`nixlUcxThreadPoolEngine` entirely, so the crashing thread never exists.

## Asks

1. **Reopen #23499.** It was closed without a fix and its 2026-07-07 follow-up is still unanswered.
2. **Document `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND_PARAMS`** in
   `docs/advanced_features/pd_disaggregation.md`. It was added in #24169 but the PD docs only
   mention `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_NIXL_BACKEND`, so the only workaround for this crash is currently
   undiscoverable without reading `environ.py`.
3. **Reconsider the hardcoded `num_threads = 8` for prefill**, or at minimum make it a documented,
   overridable knob with a note about this failure mode, until the NIXL fix lands.

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3.8 DSpark forced-reject is not lossless: accumulated GDN state drift vs Base decode
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Summary

With RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 + RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark, I can reproduce a deterministic correctness divergence between ordinary Base decode and DSpark TARGET_VERIFY even when every speculative draft token is deliberately rejected and only the target model's own argmax token is committed.

The failure is cumulative rather than context-local:

Base decode is deterministic across independent processes with a fixed seed.
Under gamma=1 forced rejection, DSpark initially matches Base but later diverges.
Rebuilding the same prefix through normal prefill restores the correct Base result at the divergence context.
Using FP32 Mamba/SSM persistent state delays the divergence substantially, but does not eliminate it.

This suggests accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift somewhere in the TARGET_VERIFY / intermediate-state / commit path.

Possibly related to the state-correctness work tracked in #34899 and #34297.

Environment

SGLang:

SGLANG_BUILD_COMMIT=c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5
SGLANG_IMAGE_TAG=lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20260814-c4271c3f
CUDA 13.0
TP=1
attention backend=triton
linear attention backend=triton

Target model:

RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4
revision:
52d1adc5f38aa5ebf099c29ed7025ba34cfbb854

Draft model:

RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark
revision:
923ed3a8572615643f0137e424e4ce4edd7f1cda

Diagnostic configuration:

max_running_requests=1
gamma=1
verify_num_draft_tokens=2
SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static
CUDA graph disabled
prefill CUDA graph disabled
seed=123456789
Triton GDN backend

Model weights are not modified.

Forced-rejection diagnostic

SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0 by itself is not a semantically valid forced-rejection test because it changes correct_len without recomputing the naturally selected target bonus token.

For gamma=1 I therefore used this local diagnostic patch in dspark_verify.py:

         if self._simulate_acc_len > 0:
-            correct_len = self._simulated_correct_len(
-                bs=bs, dtype=correct_len.dtype, device=correct_len.device
+            target_predict = torch.argmax(target_logits, dim=-1).view(
+                bs, self.verify_num_draft_tokens
             )
+            correct_len = torch.zeros_like(correct_len)
+            bonus = target_predict[:, 0]
+            cap_trim_lens = torch.zeros_like(correct_len)

The resulting request reports:

spec_accept_rate=0.0
spec_num_correct_drafts=0
spec_num_proposed_drafts=95
spec_verify_ct=95
spec_accept_histogram=[95]

Thus every first draft is rejected and the committed output token is the target model's own argmax.

Exact request

The same exact 24 input_ids are used for every run:

INPUT_IDS = [
    248045, 846, 198, 623, 799, 61446, 13901, 11,
    10033, 3069, 10583, 5802, 4833, 5983, 13, 248046,
    198, 248045, 74455, 198, 248068, 271, 248069, 271,
]

Input verification:

count: 24
SHA256:
f3d5baaf2ddb361d0d9fbff4add8071e24718908f76ae350ced01927dd87fcd0

The SHA256 is computed as:

hashlib.sha256(
    ",".join(map(str, INPUT_IDS)).encode()
).hexdigest()

Sampling:

temperature: 0
top_p: 1
top_k: -1
max_new_tokens: 96
ignore_eos: true

Example request:

payload = {
    "input_ids": INPUT_IDS,
    "sampling_params": {
        "temperature": 0.0,
        "top_p": 1.0,
        "top_k": -1,
        "max_new_tokens": 96,
        "ignore_eos": True,
    },
    "stream": False,
}
Server configuration

Relevant arguments:

sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.8-27B \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --context-length 16384 \
  --max-total-tokens 16384 \
  --max-running-requests 1 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 16 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 2048 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \
  --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \
  --disable-cuda-graph \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-draft-model-path /path/to/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 1 \
  --random-seed 123456789 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000

Environment:

SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=1.0

For the FP32-state diagnostic I additionally use:

--mamba-ssm-dtype float32
Results
1. Base oracle is deterministic

Base-only greedy decode is deterministic across independent server processes with seed 123456789.

Original BF16 Base oracle SHA256:

a935dafc6111c5acf3280bb9fa1d545f39abf5c9ba92285ba29d39949e971848
2. Original TARGET_VERIFY + forced rejection

With gamma=1, static verify, CUDA graph disabled, and the forced-rejection diagnostic:

first divergence: output index 13
Base token:   1070
DSpark token: 836

Indices 0..12 match Base.

3. Concrete beta precision mismatch

One concrete numerical difference exists between Base packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY.

Base rounds beta through the beta tensor's source dtype, while TARGET_VERIFY originally keeps the sigmoid computation in FP32.

Diagnostic patch:

-        b_beta = 1.0 / (1.0 + tl.exp(-b_b))
+        b_beta = tl.sigmoid(b_b).to(b.dtype.element_ty).to(tl.float32)

With only this change:

first divergence: 13 -> 23

Indices 0..22 now match Base.

This appears to be a real numerical contributor, but not the complete cause.

4. Fresh-prefix localization

Using the beta-aligned path, I rebuilt a fresh request consisting of:

original input IDs + exact Base output IDs [0:22]

No text was retokenized.

The request reported:

cached_tokens=0

Expected next Base tokens:

[2438, 5306]

Generated:

[2438, 5306]

Exact match.

Therefore the long-request divergence at index 23 is not a direct TARGET_VERIFY failure at that context when recurrent state is freshly rebuilt through ordinary prefill.

It requires accumulated speculative-state evolution.

5. FP32 persistent SSM state

Using the same beta alignment but changing both Base and DSpark to:

--mamba-ssm-dtype float32

results are:

FP32 Base SHA256:
5557ae475bafcb00ff5ea564e14954f5590cf8e77535edec878a7203225561fc

FP32 DSpark SHA256:
a982aa8b26b5e7f51d11669da7b42a730d839d721d0d386944c3a964321a2fcb

first divergence: index 38
Base token:   6338
DSpark token: 2279

So increasing persistent SSM precision changes:

BF16 SSM + beta alignment: index 23
FP32 SSM + beta alignment: index 38

but does not eliminate the divergence.

This suggests BF16 persistent-state storage is an error amplifier rather than the sole root cause.

6. KV precision control

With FP32 SSM and beta alignment, changing target KV cache from FP8 E4M3 to BF16 moved first divergence only:

38 -> 39

This suggests full-attention KV precision is not the primary cause of the remaining drift.

Other isolation work
Delta reduction layout

Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's delta projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation did not improve correctness:

beta + Base-layout delta projection:
first divergence = 6
Output reduction layout

Changing only TARGET_VERIFY's output projection to a literal Base [V,K] / K-axis formulation also regressed:

beta + Base-layout output projection:
first divergence = 6
Softplus expression

TARGET_VERIFY originally evaluates:

beta_x = softplus_beta * x

softplus_x = tl.where(
    beta_x <= softplus_threshold,
    (1.0 / softplus_beta) * tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(beta_x)),
    x,
)

Runtime parameters were confirmed as:

softplus_beta=1.0
softplus_threshold=20.0

Changing only this expression to Base's literal form:

softplus_x = tl.where(
    x <= 20,
    tl.log(1.0 + tl.exp(x)),
    x,
)

regressed the FP32 test:

first divergence: 38 -> 6

Because the two forms are algebraically equivalent for the actual runtime parameters, this appears to demonstrate sensitivity to Triton floating-point/codegen behavior rather than identify the root cause.

Convolution state

A source audit found persistent conv state and TARGET_VERIFY intermediate conv windows use the same default BF16 dtype and the expected post-anchor snapshot/scatter semantics for gamma=1.

Attempting the independent diagnostic:

SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float32

cannot currently be used as a clean control because the current implementation hits:

RuntimeError:
Index put requires the source and destination dtypes match,
got Float for the destination and BFloat16 for the source.
ReplaySSM

The current build exposes:

--enable-linear-replayssm-spec

but DSPARK/DFLASH explicitly rejects this path for Qwen3.8 GDN:

ValueError:
--enable-linear-replayssm-spec with DSPARK/DFLASH requires
a KDA (kimi_linear) model; got a non-KDA model.

So I could not use ReplaySSM as a GDN DSPARK correctness control.

Current hypothesis

The strongest evidence is:

forced reject + repeated TARGET_VERIFY rounds -> divergence

fresh prefill of the exact same prefix -> correct again

higher persistent SSM precision -> divergence substantially delayed

KV precision change -> almost no effect

My current hypothesis is that a small difference enters a committed/intermediate GDN recurrent state during repeated TARGET_VERIFY reject/commit rounds and accumulates until it changes the target argmax.

For gamma=1, I also audited the reject/commit indexing:

candidate row 0 = anchor/current token
commit_lens = 1
last_correct_step_indices = 0

and the committed conv window appears to correspond to the post-anchor state as expected.

The remaining high-value localization would therefore seem to be the SSM state boundary rather than further source-expression A/B tests.

Expected behavior

Under this diagnostic every speculative draft token is rejected and only the target model's own greedy token is committed.

I would expect DSpark to preserve the same greedy token sequence as ordinary Base decode.

If exact Base equivalence is intentionally not guaranteed for GDN TARGET_VERIFY because the recurrent numerical paths differ, clarification on the intended correctness invariant/tolerance would also be useful.

Questions
Is this accumulated GDN recurrent-state drift a known limitation or bug in the current DSpark TARGET_VERIFY path?
Is there an existing GDN state-commit / TARGET_VERIFY correctness patch that should be tested on this Qwen3.8 path?
Would the most useful next instrumentation be a per-layer/per-round comparison of:
Base persistent SSM state before decode
TARGET_VERIFY input persistent SSM state
TARGET_VERIFY intermediate step-0 SSM state
post-commit/scatter persistent SSM state
Is the beta source-dtype rounding difference described above expected, or should TARGET_VERIFY match Base packed decode here?
If exact Base equivalence is not expected between packed decode and TARGET_VERIFY, what correctness invariant should speculative decoding enforce for recurrent GDN models?

I can provide the exact request script, complete Base/DSpark output token arrays, hashes, and the small diagnostic source patches if useful.

### Reproduction

`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`
revision `52d1adc5f38aa5ebf099c29ed7025ba34cfbb854`

Exact request:
